newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end up, players like President's speech.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end up, players like President's speech.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed up Friday as foreign investors entered the market, encouraged by President Alberto Fujimori's claim the hostage crisis would not affect the economy, brokers said.
They added share prices were also likely to gain next week.
Friday, the General Index rose 2.24 percent to 1,461.7 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index rose 3.10 percent to 2,080.6 points.

In only his second public speech during the 16-day-old siege at the Japanese ambassador's residence, where Marxist rebels held 74 VIP hostages, Fujimori said on Thursday that the "terrorist" act was an isolated incident that would not slow the country's economic recovery.
"The speech gave both local and foreign investors confidence because they feel there is resilience in the management of the hostage crisis," said Luis Cueva of local brokerage Argos.
Brokers also said the market's rise was helped by the healthy company financial results for the January to November period of 1996 that have been published over the last two days.

Benchmark Telefonica del Peru led the market up Thursday, rising 3.60 percent to 5.18 soles on volume of 1.2 million shares. Banco de Credito closed up 0.77 percent at 3.93 soles on volume of 127,051 shares.
In a total of 1,431 trades, volume was estimated at 27.4 million soles ($10.6 million), brokers said.
